value: Anne grew up at Green Gables
unit: Anne grew up at Green Gables under the care of Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, where she pursued her studies at Avonlea School under Miss Stacy. Following a period of intense rivalry with classmate Gilbert Blythe, she prepared for and passed the entrance examinations for Queen's Academy. Upon moving to town for her studies, she was overcome with initial homesickness, which was eased by weekly trips back to Avonlea on Fridays with her schoolmates. Advised by Miss Stacy, Anne elected to take the advanced Second Year course alongside Gilbert Blythe to obtain a First Class teacher's license in one year. During her time at Queen's, she formed a close circle of ambitious friends, including Stella Maynard and Priscilla Grant, and spent spare hours visiting Miss Barry at Beechwood. Throughout her academic year, Anne worked steadily, emerging as one of the top three contenders for the academy medal and a prime candidate for the Avery scholarship.

unit: Diana Barry lived at her family's home near Green Gables, spending much of her time reading books, which her father encouraged despite her mother's concerns. When Anne Shirley arrived at Green Gables, Mrs. Barry brought Diana over to meet her in hopes of giving her a local playmate. Meeting in the garden, Anne asked Diana to be her sworn bosom friend, and Diana agreed, taking a solemn vow of friendship. The two girls quickly became inseparable companions, planning playhouses and inventing games together, such as pretending the nearby spruce grove was a Haunted Wood. On one occasion, while staying at Green Gables, Diana participated in a playful jump onto a spare-room bed, inadvertently landing on visiting Aunt Josephine Barry, who became furious; Diana steadfastly refused to blame Anne for the idea.
